Stehen × stellen e liegen × legen, passo: Stehen × stellen and liegen × legen, step by step
PASSO 1: o alemão tem DOIS verbos para c: STEP 1: German has TWO verbs for each position: one says WHERE something IS (a state, Wo?) and the other says you PUT something there (movement, Wohin?). English has the same pair with lie/lay and sit/set — German just does it for "stand" too. STEP 2: stehen (to be standing) × stellen (to put something upright). STEP 3: liegen (to be lying) × legen (to lay something down) — exactly like English lie × lay. STEP 4: the STATE verb takes the DATIVE, the MOVEMENT verb takes the ACCUSATIVE: «Die Vase steht auf dem Tisch» (the vase is on the table) × «Ich stelle die Vase auf den Tisch» (I put the vase on the table). STEP 5: the forms: stehen – stand – gestanden; stellen – stellte – gestellt; liegen – lag – gelegen; legen – legte – gelegt. Note the pattern: the state verbs are strong, the "putting" verbs are regular. STEP 6: tall things or things that stand upright (bottle, vase, lamp, chair) use stehen/stellen; flat things or things lying down (book, newspaper, key) use liegen/legen.
o português usa «estar» e «pôr» para tud: English mostly says "is" and "put" for everything: "the book is on the table", "I put the vase on the table". German asks first: is it standing or lying? That choice picks the verb pair. Your best anchor is English lie/lay and sit/set — the same old Germanic pairs.

Sitzen × setzen e hängen, passo a passo: Sitzen × setzen and hängen, step by step
PASSO 1: o mesmo par de estado e de movi: STEP 1: the same state/movement pair works for "sitting": sitzen (to be sitting, Wo?, dative) × setzen (to set, to seat someone, Wohin?, accusative) — like English sit × set: «Das Kind sitzt auf dem Stuhl» (the child is sitting on the chair) × «Ich setze das Kind auf den Stuhl» (I set the child on the chair). STEP 2: forms: sitzen – saß – gesessen (sat); setzen – setzte – gesetzt. STEP 3: «hängen» does both jobs, like English "hang": state («Die Jacke hängt an der Tür» — the jacket is hanging on the door) and movement («Ich hänge die Jacke an die Tür» — I hang the jacket on the door). In the state meaning it's strong (hängen – hing – gehangen, like hung); in the movement meaning it's regular (hängen – hängte – gehängt). STEP 4: summary: stehen/stellen (upright), liegen/legen (lying flat), sitzen/setzen (sitting), hängen (hanging).

Um grupo de substantivos masculinos ganh: A group of masculine nouns adds -n or -en in EVERY case except the nominative singular: der Student → den Studenten → dem Studenten → des Studenten. They are mostly male people and animals: der Junge (boy), der Kunde (customer), der Kollege (colleague), der Student, der Herr (gentleman, Mr.), der Mensch (human being), der Nachbar (neighbor), der Polizist (police officer), der Tourist, der Name, der Löwe (lion). Many end in -e or come from Latin/Greek with -ent, -ist, -ant. «Herr» adds only -n (den Herrn — on an envelope: «Herrn Müller»); «Name» adds -n in the accusative and dative and -ns in the genitive (des Namens). None of this applies to other masculine nouns.
